result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A's hero gives the price, the 3-month tune-up, the 3-mile pickup limit and a 'Join' button, so a commuter gets the basics before scrolling. Where proof or policy is missing, A puts a visible placeholder. Its one invented sentence, about quoting before replacing parts, is flagged for the owner to confirm. B is a clean, complete HTML page, but its hero leaves out the 3-mile limit and has no button, it adds no placeholder for missing proof, it doesn't actually answer its own 'Can I still join?' question, and it adds an unsupported 'under a minute' claim. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B's hero has the price, the 3-mile pickup limit and a join button, so a visitor gets the basics without scrolling. It also marks missing proof (customer quote, out-of-range policy, cancellation terms) with visible placeholders. Its one stretch, the promise to quote parts before replacing them, is flagged in brackets for the owner to confirm. A is a clean, honest, finished HTML page, but its top has no call to action and no 3-mile limit. It leaves gaps silently instead of marking them, and it adds a small unsupported claim ('takes under a minute') and dodges its own out-of-range FAQ question.
